Let $A$ be a connection on a bundle over a ball $B\subset\R^n$. If $\|F_A\|_{L^{n/2}(B)}$ is sufficiently small, then there exists a gauge in which $A$ is in (local) Coulomb gauge with Sobolev bounds in terms of $\|F_A\|$ \cite{UhlenbeckLp1982}. Moreover, sequences of connections with uniform $L^p$ curvature bounds (with $p>n/2$) admit subsequences converging modulo gauge away from a controlled singular set; in $4$D this underlies bubbling/compactness for Yang--Mills fields \cite{UhlenbeckLp1982,UhlenbeckRemovable1982}.\\
\textit{Assumptions.} Differential-geometric setting; small-energy hypothesis for local gauge; $p>n/2$ for compactness; typically compact structure group.\\
\textit{Limitations/barriers.} These are foundational for \emph{classical} analysis and moduli spaces (including instanton compactness), but do not by themselves provide the probabilistic/measure-theoretic control required for a quantum field theory on $\R^4$.

Let $\Lambda\subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ be a finite lattice. A (pure) lattice gauge field assigns group elements $U_e\in G$ to oriented edges $e$ with $U_{e^{-1}}=U_e^{-1}$. The Wilson action is a sum over plaquettes $p$ of a class function of the plaquette holonomy $U_p$ (product of edge variables around $p$), commonly $S_\Lambda(U)=\sum_p \Re \Tr(1-U_p)$ for matrix groups. The Gibbs measure is
\[
\mu_{\Lambda,\beta}(\mathrm{d}U) = \frac{1}{Z_{\Lambda,\beta}} \exp\!\big(-\beta S_\Lambda(U)\big)\,\prod_{e\in E(\Lambda)} \mathrm{d}U_e,
\]
with Haar measure on $G$ \cite{Wilson1974,OsterwalderSeiler1978,Seiler1982}. % Web source: lattice formulation appears in sources around Osterwalder-Seiler and Wilson. citeturn2search7turn10search0
